subject: Gateway Whitelist Decision Log & Firewall Exceptions for Private Endpoint
messages:
From: laura.kim@acme-analytics.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: trent@starlight.io
Date: 2026-11-27T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Inventory & hardening asks for Redwood private endpoint (initial)

Ben —

Thanks for the walkthrough this morning. Acme's network team needs a concise list of exactly what egress destinations and ports must be allowed from our private deployment (VPC peering + customer-managed NAT gateway) so we can update the firewall policy and run a port-scan validation.

Checklist items we need from you:
- Definitive outbound IP ranges (or FQDNs) the runtime will call for model updates/metrics/healthchecks.
- Ports/protocols and whether connections are TCP-only or require UDP.
- Any inbound paths we must open (if using callback/webhooks) and where they should terminate.
- Guidance on TLS verification and SNI requirements (so our TLS proxy doesn't break connectivity).
- Any operational exceptions (e.g., telemetry to metrics.redwood.ai) and how long they should stay open.

We ran an initial passive scan and will attach results; we want to keep the allowlist as narrow as possible for SOC/audit reasons.

Appreciate a short decision log you can share so we can attach it to the change request.

—Laura
Laura Kim
Head of Security, Acme Analytics

Attachment: acme-fw-scan-output-20261127.txt
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: laura.kim@acme-analytics.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-27T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Inventory & hardening asks for Redwood private endpoint (initial)

Laura —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Vivek (runtime/networks) and Marissa (solutions) — they will confirm precise IPs and any alternate options. High-level answers below so your change window planning can proceed:

1) Outbound destinations:
   - Control plane endpoints (for management/metrics/rollouts): prefer TLS to hostnames under *.control.redwood.ai. We provide a CSV of IPv4 ranges for customers that want IP-only allowlists.
   - Model artifact pulls: our installers may fetch model bundles from storage.redwood.ai (HTTPS).
   - Telemetry/usage: metrics.redwood.ai (HTTPS).

2) Ports/protocols:
   - TCP 443 (HTTPS) for all outbound. No UDP required for normal operation.
   - Optional: TCP 22 only if customer enables remote debug (we recommend avoid).

3) Inbound:
   - No inbound ports required for normal runtime — all requests originate from customer network to the private endpoint. If you need webhook callbacks to Acme, we'll need an egress allow and a signed callback; no public inbound to Redwood.

4) TLS/SNI:
   - SNI must be preserved for hostname-based allowlists. Our control plane terminates TLS with CA-signed certs; customers should allow SNI for *.redwood.ai to pass through TLS proxies.

I'll let Vivek & Marissa confirm the CSV of IPs and a short decision note we can attach.

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: laura.kim@acme-analytics.com, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-29T08:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Inventory & hardening asks for Redwood private endpoint (initial)

Hi Laura —

Quick technical clarifications and proposal tailored to your 'tightest' posture:

A) IP vs hostname:
   - If Acme policy disallows hostname-based allowlists (SNI passthrough not permitted), we can provide a short-lived list of stable IPv4 ranges (we rotate at most quarterly). We'll include ASN and CIDR notes to make routing easier.

B) Egress chokepoints & NATing:
   - Recommended: use a dedicated NAT gateway with static Elastic IPs (or on-prem equivalent) and route all outbound traffic from the Redwood VMs through it. This gives you a single NAT IP set to list in firewall rules and simplifies audits.

C) Ports & protocols:
   - TCP/443 only for normal ops.
   - Healthchecks: HTTPS GET to /health on control endpoints; expect 200.

D) DNS requirements:
   - Must allow DNS resolution for redwood domains. If using internal forwarding resolvers, allow outbound DNS to your recursive resolvers; no need to allow 53 to public resolvers unless your stack requires it.

E) Fallbacks & offline model pulls:
   - For customers with strict egress, we support pre-seeding model artifacts via offline transfer (scp to artifact storage path). This avoids runtime artifact pulls during model updates.

Attachment: redwood-private-gateway-ips-20261130.csv (contains curated IPs and rotation cadence).

I'll produce a short decision log PDF summarizing the recommended posture (attached). Happy to jump on a 20m call to walk the network team through this.

-Vivek
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: laura.kim@acme-analytics.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: trent@starlight.io
Date: 2026-11-30T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Gateway Whitelist Decision Log & Firewall Exceptions for Private Endpoint

Thanks Vivek — that helps a lot. A couple follow-ups from our change board: 
- We'll prefer static Elastic IPs via a dedicated NAT per Vivek's recommendation. Please confirm how many public IPs we should reserve for production (scale 3x to cover AZ drift and rolling updates).
- For the quarterly rotation: what is the notification lead time and the failover/compatibility window? We need this for our change windows.
- Telemetry destination: can you provide a hash (or fingerprint) of the certificate used by metrics.redwood.ai so our TLS proxy can pin it rather than rely solely on SNI?

Also please attach the decision log (short bullets) we can store with the change record.

—Laura
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: laura.kim@acme-analytics.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, trent@starlight.io
Date: 2026-11-30T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Gateway Whitelist Decision Log & Firewall Exceptions for Private Endpoint

Laura — thanks for the questions. Final decisions and operational notes below (this will be the PDF we attach to your change ticket).

Decision log (concise):
- Allowlist approach: Customer-managed NAT with 3 static Elastic IPs per production NAT (AZ-separated). Use those three IPs in firewall rules.
- Destination ports: TCP 443 only. No UDP. No inbound rules required.
- DNS: Allow resolution for *.redwood.ai via your internal resolvers. Do not perform TLS termination at the proxy that alters SNI.
- Certificate pinning: metrics.redwood.ai TLS cert SHA256: 9f:3b:...:a1 (full fingerprint shared via secure channel). We'll rotate certs no more frequently than quarterly; rotation notifications 21 days prior, compatibility window 14 days (both sides honor old cert).
- IP rotation cadence: IPv4 CIDR changes quarterly; we'll publish a CSV and a signed changelog. Recommended firewall workflow: accept new IPs in pre-prod validation window, then schedule prod switch.
- Offline artifact option: available; ops-level instructions in attached PDF.

Operational attachments included: redwood-private-gateway-ips-20261130.csv, decision-log-20261130.pdf.

Next steps:
1) Laura: open a firewall change with the three nat EIPs (we provided CSV sample to map to your NAT).
2) Ben: I'll create a short runbook for your network team showing the healthcheck endpoints and the telemetry cert fingerprint.
3) Vivek: confirm the signed changelog URL once uploaded.

If anyone needs a screenshare to walk the team, we can book 30m tomorrow morning.

Best —
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: decision-log-20261130.pdf, redwood-private-gateway-ips-20261130.csv
